brief.headline: Apollo posts record Q3 origination and strong inflows
bullets: Earnings & AUM: The alternatives giant’s assets under management rose to $1.07tn (£794bn) at the end of September, up 18 per cent year on year, after $53bn of inflows in the third quarter and $270bn over the past 12 months.

AI & Technology: Blackstone, which committed $9bn of its own funds to Anthropic's chip financing, told investors on October 30 that the AI company should expect a "high double-B" rating from Moody's, S P and Fitch after its Nasdaq IPO.
Family Offices & Wealth: The deal for Marietta Wealth Management comes several weeks after the firm attracted Goldman Sachs and United Bank alum Matt Humphrey to lead its integrated W-2 channel.
AI & Technology: More than 85,000 companies use Ramp to manage their business spend, giving it a unique view into where corporate dollars are actually going.

Infrastructure & Energy: A consortium led by Blackstone has agreed to invest $3.1bn in Mitsubishi Corporation's interest in the LNG Canada project, expanding the alternative asset manager's exposure to large-scale energy infrastructure, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: signals are mixed, with some markets calm and others showing strain, so expect selective risk-taking. The S&P 500 stands at 7,580.07 (down 1.8% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 21.1, an elevated reading that signals nervous markets. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.94% (down 4 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.32 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.43%, near long-run norms (down 1 bp on the prior reading).
